Solution Blueprint Draft

Invoice Exception Investigator

An agent that investigates each flagged AP invoice across SAP, Coupa and the custom vendor-risk API, chooses which checks to run, drafts a resolution and routes it to a finance approver in Teams, with a full audit trail at ~2,000 invoices/day. Recommended: a pro-code agent with MCP servers for the investigation, a Copilot Studio / Power Automate approval flow for the decision, and deterministic code for the tolerance rule and checks. Complexity: High.

Executive Summary

AP teams receive about 2,000 flagged invoices a day (NFR-02). Each needs evidence from SAP, Coupa and the custom vendor-risk API (INT-01..03), a judgement about which checks matter (FR-02), a drafted resolution (FR-07) and a finance approver's decision in Teams (FR-08, GR-01), all with a full audit trail (NFR-01).

The blueprint splits the work by type. The tolerance rule (FR-09) and the check calculations run as deterministic code, with no AI involved. The investigation and drafting is adaptive reasoning, which Stage 1 cannot confirm at this volume and audit depth, so it moves to a pro-code agent calling MCP servers. The approval is a deterministic Copilot Studio agent flow / Power Automate approval in Teams. Overall complexity is High. Most gate results are TBD until tenant, hosting and ownership facts are confirmed.

First-Draft Recommendation

Primary: Pro-code DA with MCP (25/35) for the investigation and drafting component (FR-01, FR-02, FR-07, INT-01, INT-02, INT-03, NFR-01, NFR-02). It has no failed gates. Its TBD gates are tracked as open issues.

Hybrid composition: Pro-code DA with MCP for FR-02, FR-07, INT-01..03 + Standard harness agent flow / Power Automate approval in Teams for FR-08, GR-01 + conventional rules service for FR-09 and check functions FR-03..06 + governed case store for NFR-01.

Why: the notes say the agent "decides which checks to run" across three systems, one of which is a custom API. That is the catalog's signal for adaptive reasoning, and DA + skills is not viable for it. Running unattended per invoice at ~2,000/day, with every step audited, favours a code-owned agent that writes each tool call to a governed case store. The approver gets a predictable Teams approval rather than a free-form agent conversation, which keeps reasoning separate from control.

MCP-ready: yes. SAP, Coupa and the vendor-risk API are wrapped as read-only MCP servers. If the GHCP harness is later verified in the tenant (availability, maturity, credit cost at volume, step-level audit), it could host the investigation and reuse the same servers. It is the closest alternative.

Questions to Confirm

  • Tolerance: is it variance <2% OR <$50 (a 1.9% variance on a $500k invoice auto-clears ~$9.5k), or <2% AND <$50? Does it apply to variance flags only?
  • After approval, what happens: does anything write back to SAP or Coupa (post, block, credit) and who owns that action?
  • Where do flagged invoices come from (SAP or Coupa exception queue), and what audit retention / financial-controls regime applies?

Business Problem and Opportunity

Each flagged invoice currently implies manual lookups across SAP, Coupa and the vendor-risk API before anyone can decide. At ~2,000 a day, that is a large, repetitive investigation load where the checks differ by invoice.

  • Remove trivial variances automatically under a transparent rule (FR-09).
  • Give approvers a ready, evidence-backed draft so the decision is one step (FR-07, FR-08).
  • Make every outcome auditable end to end (NFR-01).

Current State / Trigger Context

An invoice is flagged as an exception upstream (source system TBD). AP analysts currently gather context from SAP, Coupa and the vendor-risk API by hand and prepare a recommendation for a finance approver. The current tooling and cycle time are not described in the notes and are left TBD.

Target Experience / Future State

Within-tolerance variances clear automatically with a logged reason. Every other flagged invoice reaches a finance approver in Teams as a card with the drafted resolution, the checks run, their results and links to the evidence. The approver approves or rejects in one action. Anyone can reconstruct later, from the audit trail, what the agent looked at, what it concluded and who decided.

Core User Journeys

1

Auto-clear

Variance flag within tolerance (FR-09) is cleared by rule and logged. No AI, no approver.

2

Investigate

Agent plans checks, pulls SAP/Coupa/vendor-risk data, runs checks (FR-02..06, INT-01..03).

3

Decide in Teams

Approver reviews the drafted resolution and evidence, then approves or rejects (FR-07, FR-08, GR-01).

4

Audit

Every step and decision is retrievable per invoice (NFR-01).

Security, Privacy, Compliance, and Governance

  • Internal users only (SEC-01). Microsoft Entra ID assumed. No external or vendor access.
  • Least privilege: every MCP tool is read-only, and outcomes happen only through the recorded approval (GR-01).
  • Each MCP server is a security boundary with its own identity, scope, logging and rate limits.
  • Invoice and vendor text is treated as data, never as instructions, to guard against prompt injection.
  • Audit: an append-only per-case log of tool calls, inputs and outputs, checks, the draft, the approver identity and timestamps (NFR-01). Retention regime TBD.
  • Power Platform DLP governs the approval flow. The pro-code agent and MCP servers need equivalent controls owned by the build team.
  • The notes contain no personal data. Vendor data stays within the tenant's governed stores.

Primary journey sequence

Lifelines: Flag source · Intake & tolerance · Investigation agent · MCP servers & check tools · Case store / audit · Approval flow · Finance approver · AP analyst

  1. Flag source (SAP/Coupa) → Intake & tolerance: New flagged invoice event (FR-01)
  2. Intake & tolerance → MCP servers & check tools: Fetch invoice, PO, receipt amounts
  3. Intake & tolerance → Case store / audit: Open case; log flag + variance
  4. Intake & tolerance → Case store / audit: If variance flag and within tolerance: auto-clear and log rule applied (FR-09) — end
  5. Intake & tolerance → Investigation agent: Hand over case for investigation
  6. Investigation agent → Investigation agent: Plan which checks to run (FR-02)
  7. Investigation agent → MCP servers & check tools: Read SAP, Coupa, vendor-risk data (INT-01..03)
  8. Investigation agent → MCP servers & check tools: Run chosen checks: variance / duplicate / vendor risk / contract terms (FR-03..06)
  9. Investigation agent → Case store / audit: Log every tool call, input, output and check result (NFR-01)
  10. Investigation agent → Case store / audit: Save drafted resolution with cited evidence (FR-07)
  11. Case store / audit → Approval flow: Trigger approval for case
  12. Approval flow → Finance approver: Post approval card in Teams with draft + evidence (FR-08)
  13. Finance approver → Approval flow: Approve or reject, with comment (GR-01)
  14. Approval flow → Case store / audit: Record decision, approver identity and timestamp (NFR-01)
  15. Approval flow → AP analyst: Notify outcome; rejected cases return to AP analyst queue (TBD, FR-11)

Key Technical Decisions

ProposedTolerance rule (FR-09) and check calculations (FR-03..06) run as deterministic code before/alongside the agent; the LLM never decides auto-clear.
ProposedAgent and MCP tools are read-only; the only path to an outcome is the Teams approval flow (GR-01).
ProposedExpose SAP, Coupa and vendor-risk through MCP servers so the GHCP harness can reuse them if it is later verified.
ProposedEvery case event is written to an append-only governed case store, not conversation memory (NFR-01).
ProposedCode enforces a mandatory baseline check set per flag reason; the agent may add checks but not drop them.
